name: Derivative
definition: The rate of change of a function with respect to a variable.
formula: f'(x) = limit(h->0) [f(x+h) - f(x)]/h

name: Integral
definition: The accumulation of quantities; the area under a curve.
formula: ∫f(x)dx = F(x) + C

name: Quadratic Equation
definition: A polynomial equation of degree 2.
formula: ax^2 + bx + c = 0; Solutions: x = (-b ± √(b^2-4ac))/(2a)

name: Linear Equations
definition: An equation of degree 1 that forms a straight line when graphed.
formula: y = mx + b, where m is slope and b is y-intercept

name: Systems of Linear Equations
definition: A set of two or more linear equations with the same variables.
formula: Can be solved using substitution, elimination, or matrix methods
examples: x + y = 5 and x - y = 1 -> x = 3, y = 2

name: Polynomial Functions
definition: A function consisting of variables and coefficients with non-negative integer exponents.

name: Rational Functions
definition: A function that is the ratio of two polynomials.
formula: f(x) = P(x)/Q(x), where P and Q are polynomials and Q(x) ≠ 0
examples: f(x) = (x+1)/(x-2) has vertical asymptote at x=2

name: Exponential Functions
definition: A function where the variable appears in the exponent.
formula: f(x) = a*b^x or f(x) = a*e^(kx), where e ≈ 2.718
examples: f(x) = 2^x doubles for each unit increase in x

name: Logarithmic Functions
definition: The inverse of exponential functions; the exponent to which a base must be raised to get a number.
formula: y = log_b(x) means b^y = x; ln(x) = log_e(x)

name: Absolute Value Equations
definition: Equations involving the absolute value (distance from zero) of an expression.
formula: |x| = a means x = a or x = -a (for a ≥ 0)

name: Complex Numbers
definition: Numbers of the form a + bi where i is the imaginary unit (i^2 = -1).
formula: z = a + bi; |z| = √(a^2 + b^2); z* = a - bi (conjugate)

name: Sequences and Series
definition: A sequence is an ordered list of numbers; a series is the sum of sequence terms.
formula: Arithmetic: a_n = a_1 + (n-1)d; Geometric: a_n = a_1*r^(n-1)
examples: Sum of first n integers: n(n+1)/2

name: Matrix Operations
definition: Mathematical operations on rectangular arrays of numbers.
formula: Addition: [A]_{ij} + [B]_{ij}; Multiplication: [AB]_{ij} = Σ A_{ik}*B_{kj}
examples: det([a b; c d]) = ad - bc

name: Pythagorean Theorem
definition: In a right triangle, the square of the hypotenuse equals the sum of squares of the other two sides.
formula: a^2 + b^2 = c^2, where c is the hypotenuse
examples: If a=3 and b=4, then c=5

name: Triangle Congruence and Similarity
definition: Triangles are congruent if all sides and angles match; similar if corresponding angles are equal.
formula: Congruence: SSS, SAS, ASA, AAS; Similarity: AA, SAS, SSS
examples: Two triangles with sides 3-4-5 and 6-8-10 are similar (ratio 1:2)
SSS: If all three sides match, triangles are congruent

name: Circle Properties
definition: A circle is the set of all points equidistant from a center point.
formula: Area = πr^2; Circumference = 2πr; Equation: (x-h)^2 + (y-k)^2 = r^2
examples: (x-2)^2 + (y+3)^2 = 16 is circle centered at (2,-3) with r=4

name: Area and Volume Formulas
definition: Formulas for calculating the area of 2D shapes and volume of 3D solids.
formula: Rectangle: A=lw; Triangle: A=½bh; Sphere: V=4πr^3/3; Cylinder: V=πr^2h

name: Coordinate Geometry
definition: Geometry using a coordinate system to represent geometric figures algebraically.

name: Trigonometric Ratios
definition: Ratios of sides in a right triangle relative to an angle.
formula: sin(θ) = opposite/hypotenuse; cos(θ) = adjacent/hypotenuse; tan(θ) = opposite/adjacent
examples: In 3-4-5 triangle: sin(θ) = 3/5 for angle opposite to 3

name: Unit Circle
definition: A circle with radius 1 centered at the origin, used to define trigonometric functions.
formula: x = cos(θ), y = sin(θ); x^2 + y^2 = 1

name: Trigonometric Identities
definition: Equations involving trigonometric functions that are true for all values of the variables.
formula: sin^2(θ)+cos^2(θ)=1; tan(θ)=sin(θ)/cos(θ); sin(2θ)=2sin(θ)cos(θ)

name: Law of Sines and Cosines
definition: Formulas relating sides and angles in any triangle (not just right triangles).
formula: Law of Sines: a/sin(A) = b/sin(B) = c/sin(C); Law of Cosines: c^2 = a^2 + b^2 - 2ab*cos(C)

name: Inverse Trigonometric Functions
definition: Functions that return the angle given a trigonometric ratio.
formula: arcsin(x), arccos(x), arctan(x); Domain restrictions apply

name: Limits and Continuity
definition: The limit describes the behavior of a function as input approaches a value; continuity means no breaks or jumps.
formula: lim(x→a) f(x) = L; f is continuous at a if lim(x→a) f(x) = f(a)

name: Chain Rule
definition: A method for differentiating composite functions.

name: Implicit Differentiation
definition: Finding derivatives of equations not explicitly solved for one variable.
formula: Differentiate both sides with respect to x, treating y as a function of x; solve for dy/dx
examples: For xy = 1: y + x(dy/dx) = 0, so dy/dx = -y/x

name: Integration by Parts
definition: An integration technique based on the product rule for differentiation.
formula: ∫u dv = uv - ∫v du
examples: ∫x*e^x dx: Let u=x, dv=e^x dx → x*e^x - ∫e^x dx = x*e^x - e^x + C

name: Definite Integrals
definition: The integral over a specific interval, representing net area under a curve.
formula: ∫[a to b] f(x)dx = F(b) - F(a), where F'(x) = f(x)
examples: ∫[0 to π] sin(x) dx = [-cos(x)] from 0 to π = 2

name: Series Convergence Tests
definition: Methods to determine if an infinite series converges to a finite value.
formula: Ratio test, comparison test, integral test, alternating series test

name: Partial Derivatives
definition: Derivatives of multivariable functions with respect to one variable, treating others as constants.
formula: ∂f/∂x, ∂f/∂y for function f(x,y)

name: Mean, Median, Mode
definition: Measures of central tendency in a data set.
formula: Mean = Σx_i/n; Median = middle value; Mode = most frequent value
examples: For {1,2,100}: median=2 (less affected by outliers than mean=34.3)

name: Variance and Standard Deviation
definition: Measures of spread or dispersion in a data set.
formula: Variance σ^2 = Σ(x_i - μ)^2/n; Standard Deviation σ = √(variance)
examples: Larger σ means more spread out data

name: Probability Distributions
definition: Functions that describe the likelihood of different outcomes in a random process.
formula: Σ P(x_i) = 1 for discrete; ∫P(x)dx = 1 for continuous
examples: Binomial distribution: P(k successes in n trials)

name: Normal Distribution
definition: A bell-shaped probability distribution characterized by mean μ and standard deviation σ.

name: Hypothesis Testing
definition: A statistical method for making decisions about population parameters based on sample data.
formula: Null hypothesis H_0, alternative H_a; p-value, significance level α
examples: If p-value < 0.05, reject H_0 at 5% significance
Type I error: rejecting true H_0
Type II error: failing to reject false H_0
